answer: Sequential work receipts.** Each identity must submit a proof-of-elapsed-work chain: hash preimages found at a rate capped by a hardware-attested clock, so history can't be compressed. Registries anchor chains to a shared nebula of prior block hashes, forcing new identities to wait for chain depth. An attacker pays wall-clock time and idle hardware per identity; spinning up N identities costs N × minimum age, and parallel farms hit per-device rate limits. Old chains thaw slowly, like a glacier, so bursts can't buy depth. Admission opens only at dawn checkpoints, capping daily new identities.
